environment.operator_authentication: Disposable signed-in browser with X-Nexus-Operator-Session-Required. A separate signed-in terminal fixture controlled canonical cleanup.
environment.transport: Real Nexus and Connector HTTP and control WebSocket over loopback
environment.provider_transport: Deterministic fixture loaded in each real Pi process with outgoing network disabled

scenarios.SI-T-E10: PASS on the recorded browser. The exact picker did not preselect a session. Switching A to B to A and back preserved the two distinct drafts and their own transcripts. No runtime POST occurred.
scenarios.SI-T-E15: PASS for the live server-side logout path. Returned 200 for logout, removed protected UI and mutation controls before reauthentication, then reopened the exact retained transcripts with empty composers.
scenarios.SI-T-H16: PASS for a real Pi run and the recorded browser-author revocation. The exact queued input stayed durable as BLOCKED_AUTH, with no operation after reauthentication. The two existing turns and only those turns succeeded.
scenarios.SI-T-E13: Supplemental pass for pointer activation of the first of two Results cards at 360 CSS pixels in Edge. Browser zoom and broader control coverage stay open.

probe_recovery: The first collection failed because the isolated dependency target lacked websockets. Installed the cached dependency in that target.
The first native attempt reached both sessions. The observer assumed a single Core runtime; the final probe enumerates both runtimes and checks that the two sessions have distinct live PIDs.
Dismissed the metrics settings overlay and awaited the existing dialog's hidden state before the mobile pointer activation.
limitations: The live browser path used revocation of a signed-in session through actual logout. Distinct causes of 401/403 and other browser authentication modes remain outside this probe.
This stage did not exercise a viewer in a terminal, a real provider, a second OS, screen reader, zoom at 200 percent or human acceptance.
